name: Punches and boxing
pattern: Strike from a guard: the push starts in the feet and hips, the trunk turns, and the fist travels last, then snaps back to guard.
setup: Stance (right-handed): left foot forward, feet a little wider than your hips, back heel slightly raised.
Knees soft, weight even between the feet.
Guard: fists by your cheeks, elbows in front of your ribs, chin tucked.

steps.text: Relax in your stance with your hands up and chin down.
Push off the floor and turn your hips and shoulders as your fist goes straight out, turning palm down.
Hit with the first two knuckles, wrist straight, arm just short of locked.
Bring the fist straight back to your face along the same line.

cues.cue: Other hand stays at your chin.
cues.why: Dropping the non-punching hand is the most coached fault: it leaves the head open.

cues.cue: Punch from the floor: turn the back foot and hip.
cues.why: Lower body drive and trunk rotation add much of the speed and force of straight punches and hooks.

cues.cue: Snap out, snap back; do not lock the elbow.
cues.why: Elbow extension speed peaks just before impact; locking out hard strains the joint.

cues.cue: Wrist straight, fist tight at impact.
cues.why: A bent wrist on a bag is a common cause of wrist injury.

cues.cue: Chin tucked, eyes on the target.
cues.why: Protects the jaw and keeps balance.

breathing: Short, sharp breath out through the nose or mouth with each punch.

tempo.note: Rounds: commonly 2-3 minutes on, 1 minute rest.

mistakes.name: Guard drops
mistakes.looks: The non-punching hand falls toward the chest or waist.
mistakes.fix: Touch your cheek with the guard glove on every punch.
mistakes.why: Leaves you open and unbalances the stance.

mistakes.name: Elbow flares (chicken wing)
mistakes.looks: The elbow lifts out to the side before a straight punch.
mistakes.fix: Elbow down and in, fist travels in a straight line.
mistakes.why: It telegraphs the punch and slows it.

mistakes.name: Arm-only punch
mistakes.looks: Feet flat and hips square while the arm reaches.
mistakes.fix: Turn the back heel out and rotate the hip with the cross.
mistakes.why: Little force reaches the fist without the legs and trunk.

mistakes.name: Over-reaching
mistakes.looks: Head and chest lean past the front knee.
mistakes.fix: Step closer; nose stays behind the front toes.

safety: Wrap your hands and wear bag gloves for bag work.
Start bag work gently; full-power punches on a bag stress wrists and knuckles.
Shoulder pain: shorter rounds and less snap on full extension.

variants.change: Heavy bag work: about 5.8 MET (15110). At 60, 120, 180 punches a minute: about 7.0, 8.5, 10.8 MET.
Shadow boxing or a simulated round: about 9.3 MET (15125).
Pad work with a partner: oxygen use is close to sparring (sparring about 7.8 MET, 15120).
Band or cable from behind adds resistance to the push; slower, strength-focused.
Seated: only the arms and trunk turn; low-impact cardio.
Punches combined with another move; keep the guard rules.
Defence drill: forearms and gloves cover the head, no strike.

subtypes.name: Cross
subtypes.change: Rear hand straight punch: back heel turns out, hips and shoulders rotate fully.

subtypes.name: Hook
subtypes.change: Elbow lifts to shoulder height, arm bent about 90°, fist swings across on a horizontal arc as the trunk turns.

subtypes.name: Uppercut
subtypes.change: Dip the knees a little, then drive up: the bent arm rises on a vertical arc, palm facing you.

subtypes.name: Block and guard
subtypes.change: Hold a tight guard; forearms lift to cover the head, small knee dips.

easier: shadow boxing at an easy pace
harder: bag rounds at 120-180 punches a minute

metrics.label: Elbow out to the side on straight punches
Trunk turn on cross and hook

motion.basis: Default loop is a left jab (orthodox stance, left-side keys). Punch types and speeds from piorkowski2011 and whiting1988; trunk and lower-body contributions from dinu2020 and lowerlimb2025; phases from lenetsky2020. Joint angles are estimates. METs from the 2024 Compendium (herrmann2024) and bag VO2 data in arseneau2011.
